renders._yaml:
- component: card
  id: neoepitope_count
  title: Candidate neoepitopes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of candidate neoepitopes Neo scored, with the number of distinct genes behind them, and the bars rank the event types that create them. It answers how large the neoepitope pool is and which kind of event feeds it.
    How to read: compare the event types to see which of them contribute most. Very few candidates point to a quiet tumor or to missing inputs, so check the variant calls and the HLA typing first.
    Note: Neo predicts neoepitopes from DNA events only and uses RNA to weigh them, not to find them.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/neo/README.md
  column: gene
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: variant_type
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: candidates, by event type
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: neoepitope_tpm_spread
  title: Expression of the candidates
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median effective expression of the candidates, with the lowest and highest value beside it. It answers whether the candidates sit in genes that are expressed in the tumor.
    How to read: a median near zero means most candidates are silent, so few of them can be presented. Effective expression is long-tailed, so the range matters more than the centre when you pick candidates to follow up.
    Note: effective expression is estimated by Neo from the sample's RNA transcript expression and the cohort median expression, and is empty when no RNA was run.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/neo/README.md
  column: effective_tpm
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: median, with its range

- component: figure
  id: neoepitope_source_bar
  title: Candidates by event type
  description: |-
    Each bar counts the candidate neoepitopes created by one kind of event (missense, frameshift, in-frame indel or fusion), split by tumor. It answers which events the neoepitope pool comes from.
    How to read: a pool made almost entirely of one event type is expected when that event dominates the tumor's mutations. Compare tumors to spot one whose mix differs, then open the table to inspect its candidates.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: variant_type
    color: sample
    labels:
      variant_type: Event type
      sample: Tumor

- component: advanced_viz
  id: neoepitope_expression_scatter
  title: Copy number against expression
  description: |-
    Each point is a candidate neoepitope: the copy number of the variant behind it on the horizontal axis and its effective expression on the vertical axis, coloured by event type. It answers which candidates come from variants that many tumor cells carry and that are also expressed.
    How to read: points in the upper right are the strongest candidates to follow up, since the variant is present in most copies and the gene is expressed. Points on the floor are not expressed, so their peptides are unlikely to be presented. Open the table to inspect the labelled genes.
    Note: Neo weighs each candidate's presentation likelihood by its expression. No cut-off is drawn on either axis, because none is sourced.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/neo/README.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Copy number of the variant
    y_title: Effective expression (TPM)
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    x: variant_copy_number
    y: effective_tpm
    label: gene
    color: variant_type

- component: table
  id: neoepitope_table
  title: Neoepitope candidates
  description: |-
    Each row is a candidate neoepitope: the event that creates it, its gene, the novel amino acids between their flanks, the number of peptides it yields, its RNA support, its expected and effective expression and the copy number behind it. It answers which candidates to follow up and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by effective expression, then filter by event type. A candidate with RNA fragments and a high copy number is better supported than one found in the DNA alone.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: neoepitope_id
